verdict.tagline: A timeless shooter classic that still delivers, despite its age.
for_you_if: you want to experience a foundational first-person shooter
you appreciate classic level design and atmosphere

you find quicksaving and save management frustrating
you cannot tolerate dated graphics and controls

When this game was first released in 1998, I must have played it at least 5 times through in the first couple of months. Today, we are so accustomed to FPS games that give total immersion with storyline and world building, but before 1998, none of these things had been refined. Then Half Life came along, and that opening tram ride with no action, just a 5 minute ride through the world, not to mention the inciting incident in the test chamber, absolutely blew up my expectations of what an FPS could deliver. 

I popped the game open yesterday, and while the technicals of the game are rough around the edges due to it being a nearly 30 year build of a game, the craftsmanship of this game are still absolutely apparent. A total masterpiece

cohorts.summary: Reviewers highlight dated visuals, slippery movement, and platforming hazards alongside save system pitfalls.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the movement feels slippery, with the character controlling like a ball on ice.

citations.review_text: Just finished my first playthrough, in 2026. It's...a complicated matter. On the one had, I can see the potential of the game and it is very clear that it was made with lots of love, on the other hand...it's a frustration festival. Freeman controls like a ball on ice, the game throws many surprises so you will load the game a lot and there is basically no story at all. Still, it will get a thumbs up, it's Valve after all (please don't delete my account, my overlords).

I was very excited to finally play such an important piece of videogame history, but despite its undeniable influence and a number of cool ideas, I just can't get over the things that aged like milk.
The movement in this game is so infuriating. The level design flip flops between brilliant and horrible. The audio is torture. There are so many little things that make this game *feel* old.

I can't lie: I did not have a good time playing this.

Half-Life is such an iconic game filled to the brim with memorable encounters, enthralling world building, and an impressively realized world for a game nearing 30. 


Xen is an absolute trainwreck and destroys any goodwill the first 70% of this game establishes.

I used to think it was just a gameplay shift thing people weren't ready for. Or some kind of difficulty spike. Or some kind of half-baked unfinished levels that lacked the creativity of the rest of the game. I just didn't think it would be all of them at once. I played this game entirely blind, up until Xen where I had to stop every 5 minutes to look up how to get out of a room, how to evade an enemy, HOW TO LAND WITHOUT TAKING FALL DAMAGE. 

Half-Life is a classic and definitely worth playing, but Xen is going to keep me far away from ever replaying this. It's that bad.

Firstly, and most crucially: The game is a relic of its time. I think every issue I had with the game—unclear paths, bugs, and janky controls—is just a consequence of the game being a revolutionary title from 1998.
However, the “unclear paths” point brings me to my biggest takeaway from this game’s design: it forces you to be immersed in order to succeed. You need to think for yourself, try everything, and let people live if you want to receive their assistance. You aren’t just told exactly what to do at every moment and handheld down a path, like so many games do today. You need to figure out how to escape Black Mesa on your own. To that end, the game’s demanding of your immersion and concentration is probably my favorite thing about it.
I looked up what to do several times, but in my opinion, every time I didn’t know where to go was just me being an idiot, except for two different occasions: first, me not obtaining a pistol at the start of Waste Processing because I didn’t follow the guard, leading me to do the whole chapter without it before googling the pistol’s location and restarting the chapter; and second, the flooding of the Lambda Core bugging so that it didn’t fill all the way because I turned the two valves in quick succession. Because of those two incidents, the only two changes I would make to this game are to have the guard die to the headcrabs he’s fighting, and to fix that bug with the flooding.
Sure, the game sometimes aggravated me or bored me, but I cannot in good faith say that any other part of this game could be changed without worsening the final product overall. The game’s goal is to immerse you into its world and make you feel the exact amounts of fear, tension, and power that Freeman himself would feel; it accomplishes that pretty much flawlessly. After finally beating Half-Life for the first time, I get why it’s a legendary classic.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features dated graphics and visual elements.

citations.review_text: I've been putting off this game series for a looooong time I decided i'd give it a shot after i bought my steam machine. Well that time has come and WOW I did not realize how much I was missing out on I enjoyed every minute of it. If you've never played Half Life before give it a shot this game was a treat. If you can make it passed the dated graphics, the game is a 10 out of 10. from the atmosphere to the story and the game play it really is great. And now I see why people revere this game as one of the best. I'm moving on to HL2 now. Then after that i'll likely be walking on to the cope train destination HL3. All in all an amazing game. And the controller support was not bad very seamless.

[i]Half-Life[/i], even for its older age caught me off guard initially. I definitely expected something cool, adventurous, and sci-fi-- not the eerie horror of watching your coworkers get slaughtered in front of you, and that definitely roped me in. The light puzzling and fps gameplay, paired with the dated visuals actually work in its favor in that regard, adding to that unsettling atmosphere. Shooting aliens and the 'bad guys' is just plain fun, there are genuinely neat cinematic moments, and its easy to see why it was genre defining. I'm still decently shocked by how dynamic the world and dialogue feels for a late-90s game with the hardware limitations. Valves push for cutting edge showed even then. The mystery of the story is compelling too, unraveling in front of you as you move through the facility alongside Gordon himself, and the variety of environments and enemies (visually interesting but sometimes horribly annoying, like those floating brainlet guys near the end), kept tings interesting. 

That said, I'd land this in the middle-of-the-road to slightly above average. The "old game syndrome" with this one really drags it down. There's the random difficulty spikes, jank, dated saving that sometimes screws you because you forgot to 10 minutes ago, and sometimes dumb puzzles (the tentacle monster, or the random drainage pipe I missed sitting in a crack somewhere) that eat up time more than I would like sometimes. Visually I think its also rough in some places, especially in the late-game areas, which had this uncanny, veiny, almost gross texture that makes my neck itch for some reason. It just came off as ugly to me, and not in the good way it was probably intended at the time, not aging too well. There are tons of hidden secrets, but between the jank and frustration, I don't see myself replaying it anytime soon. I can see how a kid in the late 90s with nothing else to play would've had a blast, but that's not where we are now. For as much as I love it, I thin…

The one that started it all. Half-Life hardly needs an introduction, it forever changed FPSs as we know them. The graphics are absolutely dated, but there's something to its chunkiness that adds to the industrial toxic atmosphere of Black Mesa Research Facility.

Classic game which is still worth playing to this day. 

I've been getting into Half Life as of late for the first time, growing up my only exposure to it being through Gmod and SFM. I started the game about a Year and a half ago and was about halfway through it until I switched computers and the game deleted my save file. 

I decided to try and pick it back up again a few days ago and just finished it half an hour or so ago as of writing this review. I'll try and avoid any major spoilers as the game is best seen through experience. 

Don't let the outdated graphics and goofy dialogue fool you, this game is a great time. It can be a bit janky from time to time but nothing immersion breaking, this game is extremely immersive with its story telling. Pretty much never taking away control from the player, allowing you to feel like you are actually apart of the world and affecting it with your own actions instead of being a vessel for another character. The gameplay is super fun, mixing strategic gunplay with logic based puzzle solving. 

Most of the puzzles feel simple enough to understand but not so easy that it doesn't feel rewarding from completing them. Allowing for progression to feel smooth and well paced. My only real complaint with the game is final few chapters which were a bit of a downgrade compared to the rest of the game but was worth it for the ending. I recommend this game to anybody who wishes to try it out or get into the Half Life franchise, 100% worth your time.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the extensive use of quicksaving and save scumming as necessary strategies to get through challenging sections on a first playthrough.

citations.review_text:
Having been a long time fan of Doom 3 and Half-Life 2 on the original Xbox, I can really see the inspiration half-life had/has on redefining first person shooter adventure games. You feel like a parkour master after a while, but you are 100% save scumming on certain parts your first playthrough.
I highly recommend this game, especially if you are new to mouse and keyboard gaming, like me.

Pretty good game for when it was released. 
Decent graphics and sound, surprising amount of gameplay, and quite difficult at that. 

Thank goodness for quicksaving.

The only problem is the stupid [spoiler] laser warehouse [/spoiler] level. 
Definitely worth the price, and almost always on sale. 
The main reason to play this game though, is so that you're familiar with the story to play Half-Life 2.

Playing this game is like travelling in time. 28 years after its release, it carries ideas that were considered extraordinary then and surprisingly seem fun still. Playing the game on hard was challenging but not impossible. The gunplay has dated a bit but the story is still beautiful. I personally liked all of the alien experiences through the game. Saving frequently helps as does exploring every area for extra loot. Overall, fun to experience albeit the aging graphics. 3/5
